Data & method

How the Lahore Canyon is built

Two 1.2 × 1.2 km areas on a 4 m grid: the Walled City around Rang Mahal, and DHA Phase 2. Every outside wall is cut into storey-high panels, and every roof and street cell is a surface. For each one, the model works out how much open sky it sees, whether it is in direct sun at each hour (by tracing the sun's rays across the 3D buildings), and how hot it gets from sun, air temperature, wind and the heat given off by its surroundings. The "What if" options rerun that calculation in your browser.

Data

  • Building heights: Google Open Buildings 2.5D Temporal, 2023 layer, 4 m resolution. Dataset
  • Surface temperature and vegetation: Landsat 8 Collection 2 Level-2, scene 149/038, 7 Jun 2026 10:35 PKT, via Microsoft Planetary Computer. Dataset
  • Hourly weather (air temperature, humidity, sunshine, wind, height of the mixing layer): ERA5 reanalysis via the Open-Meteo archive. API
  • PM2.5: CAMS air-quality model via Open-Meteo. These are model estimates, not station readings. API
  • Landmark names: © OpenStreetMap contributors. Licence

Checked against the satellite

The model was compared with two satellites. One setting was tuned against Landsat: how much sunlight surfaces absorb (walls 0.69, roofs 0.81, ground 0.92, typical of brick, plaster and dusty asphalt). Afternoon cooling by rising hot air uses ERA5's boundary-layer height.

CheckAreaModelSatellite
Landsat 8, 7 Jun, 10:35 am, 30 mWalled City51.3 °C51.6 °C
DHA Phase 249.1 °C50.1 °C
MODIS Aqua, 10 Jun, 4:30 am, 1 kmWalled City28.5 °C27.1 °C
DHA Phase 228.8 °C27.6 °C
MODIS Aqua, 10 Jun, 2:48 pm, 1 kmWalled City62.7 °C42.3 °C
DHA Phase 260.2 °C44.1 °C

Morning and night agree within about 1.5 °C. The afternoon does not: the model is far hotter than MODIS. Part of the gap is the sensor (MODIS averages 1 km and also reads about 10 °C below Landsat in the morning), but MODIS also shows surfaces warming only 1–3 °C between morning and afternoon, while the model warms them much more. So the afternoon figures in this app are upper estimates. The patterns (which surfaces, floors and streets are hotter than others) are the reliable part.

What is measured and what is modelled

Every temperature in degrees shown in this app is measured or comes from weather records: Landsat 8 and MODIS for the ground surface, ERA5 for the air. No satellite can measure a single wall or roof, so for those the model is used only to compare: which surfaces, floors and streets run hotter or cooler than others, and by roughly how much. Sun and shade, hours of sun and sky share are calculated directly from the real building heights and the sun's position.

Limits

  • Air temperature and wind come from one 9 km ERA5 cell, the same for both areas. The app maps surface heat, not the air temperature a person feels.
  • Building heights are machine-learning estimates. Lanes narrower than about 4 m are not resolved.
  • Night-time figures are model results; the satellite check is daytime only.
  • "How fast smog can clear" is based on how open each street is to the sky. It is not a pollution simulation.
  • Floor space stands in for residents; no population data was used.
